transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-07
Time: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~58m
Attendees: Alexei Martin, Priya Nair, Samir Desai — Redwood; Evan Soto, Maya Chen, Luis Gomez, Hannah Park — NovaHealth

Summary: Quick intake for Optimize sandbox focused on quantization sensitivity and round-trip fidelity; demo of console heuristics for INT8/FP8 tradeoffs; discuss data security (VPC, KMS), rollout plan and benchmarks to validate latency vs quality.

Topics: intro + objectives; current infra; fidelity targets; demo: Optimize sandbox + qprofile picker; example sensitivity tests; rollout/canary; next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alexei: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll run 50 minutes, go through the Optimize sandbox intake — quick intro, then Priya will walk through the console and the qprofile flows, then we'll scope a short lab.
[00:07] Evan: cool thanks, Alexei. we want to understand how far we can push INT8 for our triage model without introducing hallucinations — latency target is sub-220ms at 95th pct, cost target is under $0.006 /k token — rough numbers.
[00:21] Priya: great, quick clarifying q: is that 220ms server-side only or includes network roundtrip?
[00:26] Luis: that's server-side only, network is separate — we're sticking behind a VPC in GCP.
[00:31] Priya: ok that helps. also curious about your model family and prompt length distribution — those shape qprofile picks.
[00:36] Maya: model's a 13B transformer, few-shot prompts average 120 tokens input, responses average 180 tokens; we have a high-sensitivity clinical QA path (EHR snippets) and a lower-sensitivity summarization path.
[00:47] Alexei: good—so two workloads, one safety-critical. we'll demo using a copy of your short QA prompt set, but for intake please upload 4–5 representative prompts and 200 eval pairs as Maya mentioned.
[00:59] Evan: can you walk through how Optimize chooses INT8 vs FP8? we heard FP8 gives better fidelity but higher variance?
[01:05] Priya: sure — at a high-level, Optimize runs a sensitivity sweep across bitwidth and quantization recipes. INT8 typically reduces memory and compute but sometimes drops accuracy at rare tokens; FP8 keeps dynamic range which helps on sensitive tokens. our console shows a heatmap where we plot degradation risk vs latency gain.
[01:23] Priya: i'll share screen — apologies if the window name shows "Redwood Optiimize" (laughs) — this is the sandbox.
[01:30] [screen share noise]
[01:38] Priya: here is the qprofile picker, you can load a model variant, then upload eval set; the sampling mode lets us run batch microbenchmarks and behavioral tests — we run both token-level KL and end-task F1.
[01:49] Maya: is the eval run deterministic? we need reproducible numbers for compliance.
[01:53] Priya: yes — when you pin the seed and the config we log the run id; sandbox stores traces and we persist thresholds. note that due to some backend batching nondeterminism there can be small jitter — we log and show confidence bands.
[02:06] Samir: also we tie telemetry to the KV cache and prefix cache stats — sometimes the biggest gains are from prefix caching, not bitwidth.
[02:14] Evan: what's the real-world impact? can you show a before/after for a sample prompt?
[02:18] Priya: will do — run 3 configs: FP16 baseline, INT8 qprofile A, FP8 qprofile B.
[02:24] [benchmark run noise ~ 10s]
[02:36] Priya: results: baseline 95th p latency 310ms, INT8 A 95th p 210ms, FP8 B 95th p 250ms. quality: baseline F1 0.89, INT8 A 0.86, FP8 B 0.885. so INT8 gives biggest latency wins but a 3 point drop in F1 on that set.
[02:57] Maya: hmm 3 points on clinical QA is big. is there a way to fallback per-prompt?
[03:01] Priya: yes — Optimize supports adaptive rollouts: we can enable per-route fallback rules so if a prompt triggers a high-uncertainty signal (logit entropy or a critic score) we route to FP16 or FP8. that keeps the tail safe but preserves cost.
[03:13] Hannah: about security — does sandbox data live in our VPC? are keys managed by us?
[03:18] Alexei: good question — we offer a private sandbox option with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS; for the hosted sandbox we redact and encrypt, but for regulated EHR we recommend private. we'll send the whitepaper.
[03:31] Evan: how quick is a rollback if fidelity degrades after rollout?
[03:35] Priya: rollbacks are immediate — we have automatic fallback and can pin to baseline; in Dedicated we can also hot-swap model variants. we also track quality regression alerts tied to your eval set so you get notified before major user impact.
[03:46] Luis: network-wise we'll need peering and firewall rules; do you support private peering and SAML SSO?
[03:51] Samir: yes SAML SSO for the console, and VPC peering options; we'll include a template.
[03:56] Evan: how are costs reported? we need token-level breakdown per route.
[04:00] Alexei: Console shows per-route token spend, batching efficiency, and a per-model unit cost estimate; Optimize will also recommend batch size and KV cache TTL to meet cost targets.
[04:08] Maya: curious about sensitivity testing: how do you generate the stress cases that reveal worst-case hallucination?
[04:12] Priya: we provide adversarial perturbation tools and a human-in-the-loop harness — you can seed with known failure modes. we also do a randomized prefix distortion sweep. for today we'll demo a targeted perturbation set.
[04:25] [demo run ~ 12s]
[04:38] Priya: interesting — INT8 A tripped on a long numeric table prompt; FP8 preserved schema. that aligns with the general pattern: low-bitwidth struggles on long-range numeric dynamics.
[04:49] Maya: can we get per-token attribution so we can see where it went wrong?
[04:52] Priya: yep we send attention scores and token-level logit diffs in the trace; trace export goes to your S3 or GCS and we show a quick diff view in console. there is occasional transcription of model internals as 'KV cash' — but it's KV cache actually.
[05:06] Evan: what about mixed precision — like keep attention in FP8 but weights INT8?
[05:10] Priya: we support hybrid profiles; Optimize can search hybrid configs. often hybrid gives most of the latency wins with smaller quality drop.
[05:18] Alexei: let's talk rollout cadence — recommend small canary at 1% traffic for 48 hours, telemetry gating, then step up to 10%, 25% with auto-rollback. we can run that in Dedicated or Hosted with routing policies.
[05:31] Luis: last question on telemetry retention and audit logs for SOC2 — how long do you retain traces?
[05:36] Samir: default is 90 days for traces with options for longer retention for enterprise. audit logs can be integrated into your SIEM via secure forwarding.
[05:45] [short pause]
[05:47] Evan: ok this looks promising — for next week we want the sandbox, the sensitivity checklist and a 2 hour lab. can we confirm dates?
[05:54] Alexei: we'll aim to deliver sandbox invites by Friday 10th, kickoff lab week of 13th — I'll send a calendar invite after this call.
[05:59] Priya: quick note: when you upload the eval pairs, try to include edge cases — numeric tables, long context with citations, and the short clinical prompts. we'll use those to build the qprofile heatmap.
[06:10] Maya: ack. one more: do you have examples of rollback thresholds? i'd like numeric examples.
[06:14] Priya: yes — typical gating: task F1 drop >1.5% or KL divergence >0.05 on the eval set triggers auto-rollback. we'll surface suggested thresholds and you can tune.
[06:25] Alexei: sweet. last recap: action items listed in the runbook. thanks for the time.
[06:30] Evan: thanks all.

End of call.
